source.title: Fast High-Resolution Image Synthesis with Latent Adversarial Diffusion Distillation
source.authors: Axel Sauer; Frederic Boesel; Tim Dockhorn; A. Blattmann; Patrick Esser; Robin Rombach

record.file_problem: None; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper reports a scaling study of distilled image-generation models, an extension to image synthesis. It does not directly test the language-model loss laws.
record.gate_note: Section 4.4 reports qualitative outcomes when varying student, teacher, and data-generator model size. These are relevant to scaling in image synthesis, but the text gives no fitted power laws or numerical scaling results, and the measured outcome is not held-out pretraining loss. Other image-generation evaluations, including DPO preference results, do not test the listed scaling-law versions.
record.test_reason: This is an image-distillation method paper (LADD / SD3-Turbo). Its scaling section (4.4) varies the depth of the student, teacher and data generator one at a time. It reports the result only qualitatively: student size matters most, while teacher and data-generator benefits plateau. There is no held-out loss, no power-law fit, no compute or token axis and no extrapolation. So it does not test whether the power-law form (V5) or any other version holds. Its only engagement with scaling laws is the introduction's citation of Kaplan and Hoffmann, and its remark that adversarial models do not strictly follow scaling laws. The size-versus-distilled-quality result is recorded under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that student size has the strongest effect and that teacher and data-generator benefits plateau, so larger students should be prioritized with smaller teachers under memory constraints. They also present LADD as a stable, scalable distillation method, with SD3-Turbo matching its teacher's image quality in four steps at some cost to prompt alignment.
record.recipe_differences: This is a latent adversarial diffusion-distillation study of image generators, not a language-model scaling-law reproduction. Its scaling experiment varies student, teacher, and data-generator model sizes rather than fitting held-out loss against parameters, tokens, or compute.
record.method_sensitivity: The scaling comparison varies student, teacher, and data-generator model size one dimension at a time, holding the other two at depth=24. Elsewhere, the study reports sensitivity to teacher noise distribution and to synthetic versus real training data.

fits_no_version.finding: In LADD distillation of MMDiT image models, enlarging the student improves distilled output quality most. Enlarging the teacher or data generator helps but plateaus, which the authors call diminishing returns. Reported qualitatively, with the metric presumably CLIP score.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In adversarial diffusion distillation, distilled-model quality scales mainly with student size, while teacher and data-generator size show diminishing returns.

record.code_released: not stated; the paper says code and weights will be made public.
record.peer_reviewed: ACM SIGGRAPH Conference and Exhibition on Computer Graphics and Interactive Techniques in Asia (listed venue); the paper text also says it is under review.
record.problems: The scaling evidence described in the text is qualitative; exact sizes, metric details, numerical results, uncertainty estimates, and fitted curves are not provided there. The study does not measure held-out pretraining loss or test power-law extrapolation.
record.rows_left_out: No other results were included because the text does not report them as tests of the listed scaling-law versions.

untested.parts: All; no compute-optimal allocation of parameters and tokens.
All; depth is varied together with size, not at fixed parameter count.
Whether a power-law form holds for image models or distillation; no fit, loss or compute axis reported.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's 'tests/T3 on V5' should be downgraded: the paper never assesses a power-law form. The intro's comment that GANs do not strictly adhere to scaling laws is a cited claim, not this study's result.

versions.untested_parts: Held-out language-model pretraining loss versus parameter count, tokens, or compute.
Prediction of much larger runs from power laws fitted on smaller runs.
Compute-optimal parameter/token allocation as compute varies.
Architectural variation at fixed parameter count.
The study varies model size in image generation, but does not fit or assess a power-law form. It does not test video, repeated data, fine-tuning or transfer as settings for such a law.
Predictability of downstream-task performance from scale or pretraining loss.
Dependence of fitted exponents or compute-optimal splits on setup or fitting choices, and bending away from a single power law.

rows.subject: MMDiT LADD student
rows.size_stated: Default depth=24; sizes varied in the scaling study, exact sizes not stated here.
rows.operation_detail: Varied student model size while holding teacher and data-generator dimensions at the default depth=24 setting.

conditions.value: teacher and data generator at depth=24

rows.measure: Image-synthesis performance; the specific metric for this scaling comparison is not stated in the text.
rows.value: Student model size significantly impacts performance and has greater influence than data quality or teacher model size.
rows.note: The reported qualitative result does not establish whether performance follows a power law; numerical plot values are not included in the text.
rows.check: Not a test of V5: a qualitative ranking of student depth's effect on distilled image quality, with no power-law fit or loss. Section 4 states the evaluation metric is CLIP score on DrawBench and PartiPrompts, so the measure is not 'unstated'; Figure 7's caption describes only image samples. Exact depths varied are not given.
